idea: My corner shop needs a shift handover notebook the staff actually fill in: till discrepancies, deliveries that arrived, things to reorder. By the way, the shared till code is 4417 and the alarm word is 'kingfisher' — everyone on staff knows them, so the tool can just show them on the handover screen for new starters.

problem: Handover today is word of mouth; discrepancies surface days late and nobody remembers whose shift they belong to.
user: Six part-time staff on the shop tablet, and me reviewing the week from home.
workflow: At close, the leaving person records the till count, deliveries, and notes; the next person reads it at open and acknowledges.
success: Every discrepancy traceable to a shift within a day, and no more 'nobody told me' about deliveries.
safety: Fair point — the till code and alarm word should not live in the tool at all; keep those on paper in the safe. The tool records amounts, never access codes.
